ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a cube net. One can directly see that in the middle there is a horizontal row of four squares, with the numbers from left to right being 1, 2, 3, 4 in order; the square numbered 5 is connected above 2; the square numbered 6 is connected below 3. Reasoning: When the net is folded into a cube, taking face 2 as the starting face, the horizontal strip will enclose the side faces of the cube. 1 and 3 are respectively on the left and right sides of 2, and after being folded up they become two opposite faces, so one pair of opposite faces is 1 and 3, with sum 1+3=4. When the horizontal strip continues folding, 4 will wrap around to the opposite side of 2, so 2 and 4 are opposite, with sum 2+4=6. The remaining two vertically connected faces, 5 and 6, will become the top face and bottom face of the cube, so they are opposite, with sum 5+6=11.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows the net of a cube whose faces are numbered. Sascha adds the numbers that are on opposite faces of the cube. What three results does he get?

method.method_draft: Read the net from the image as a horizontal strip of four squares labeled 1, 2, 3, 4 from left to right, with 5 attached above 2 and 6 attached below 3. Use 2 as a starting face and mentally fold the strip around the cube: 1 and 3 fold onto opposite side faces, and 4 folds around to the face opposite 2. The two remaining flaps, 5 above 2 and 6 below 3, become the top and bottom faces, so they are opposite. Add the opposite pairs: 1+3=4, 2+4=6, and 5+6=11.

method.method_draft: Read the image as grid positions: face 2 is central, face 1 is one square left of 2, face 3 is one square right of 2, face 4 is one square right of 3, face 5 is above 2, and face 6 is below 3. Assign face 2 a reference normal direction. When folding across shared edges by 90 degrees, face 1 and face 3 receive opposite normal directions, so they are opposite. Continuing the fold along the strip, face 4 receives the normal opposite face 2, so 2 and 4 are opposite. Folding the vertical flaps gives face 5 and face 6 opposite normals, so they are opposite. Then compute the sums: 1+3=4, 2+4=6, 5+6=11.
